evidence: Frozen bytes verified: sha256 of task/instruction.md = 256c5b5d...38c9b9, hireops_rules.md = b61445e8...4b7f, integration.md = 1b56dd3f...352c, all equal to qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r4/manifest.json lines 11-13. (1) Skill-prescribed grep over instruction.md + environment/instructions/*.md for judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel plus gate|probe|verif|grade|grading|polish|visual|functional|scored|test|harbor|oracle|CHANGE_ME|TODO|{{|canary returned only two benign hits: instruction.md:13 'expose GET /api/health as a check that never touches the database' (product health endpoint, also a public runtime requirement) and hireops_rules.md:172 'as soon as the workspace notices' (substring 'notices'). No judge/model name, no rubric/criterion/dimension/weight wording, no test path (/tests, /logs/verifier), no scoring.toml or score.py, no Playwright/restart_app tooling mention. (2) Criterion ids (hro_gate_render, hro_gate_shared, scored ids) and dimension names (functional/polish/visual, gates) do not appear in the brief or notes. No GATE-PROBE-style literal exists: the judges create their own unique titles/names at run time (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23, tests/scored/*/prompt.md:11 'unique title (add a short suffix for this review)'), and none is pre-named in the brief. (3) Verbatim-overlap scan: tokenised 10-grams of the public brief+notes vs all 286 string fields of every judge.toml plus every prompt.md and app_context.md found exactly one shared 10-gram, in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml criterion[20].description: 'arrive at the bottom of that stage in board order' which is the criterion restating the public rule hireops_rules.md:90 — that is the criterion quoting the brief (correct direction for fairness), not criterion text leaked into the brief. (4) Product view names 'Board, Conversations and Activity' (instruction.md:11) are product surfaces, not grader dimensions. (5) integration.md differs from the template only by the added delivery/symlink paragraph (lines 16-19), which is runtime packaging guidance in product terms and names no grader. Environment Dockerfile copies only instructions/ and assets/ (no tests/ or solution/). Counterexample attempts: a broken app cannot exploit anything here because the brief exposes no probe value, criterion wording, or grader sentinel to hard-code; a conforming alternative is not penalised by anything this row governs. This is a static source row; no runtime measurement is required for it, and none was run (no Docker, no checker executable). Manual application, not a portal check-instruction-hygiene.py run.
